question.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=4t \\ z=7\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
question.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4t \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

question.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

question.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ 5-4t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t \\ -4t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-2,5,\frac{1}{7})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/1ffc0945ea74b1bd467a0b9935ee28b88be004c18b11492d67ecdfec56e1bb09.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
question.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
question.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(7,-11,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$
